f.title: The file key still takes the FIRST year before ACE, not the year right before it, so a date or cycle tag ahead of the estimate's year files the estimate under that year (meeting another year's locked-replace question)
f.area: RV1 file key (R05/R11 fix)
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html importAce(): `/(?:^|\D)(20\d\d)(?!\d)(?:.*?[^A-Za-z])?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i`. The lazy `.*?` lets any text, including another year, sit between the captured year and ACE. The comment above it says 'and still the year RIGHT before ACE'.
f.scenario: The board holds the approved, locked 2027ACE. The person imports the 2026 estimate saved as 'PB2027 2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx'. They are asked to replace the LOCKED 2027ACE with it. If they press OK, the approved 2027 estimate is gone and 2027ACE holds the 2026 figures (FY2027 $0, FY2026 $1,000,000). 'BES2028 from 2026 ACE.xlsx' is silently filed as a new 2028ACE, and '2025-11-03 2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx' as 2025ACE. Each is a second estimate of 2026, and spAce moves to it. v2.11's pattern filed 'BES2028 from 2026 ACE' correctly as 2026ACE. Expected: each of these is 2026ACE, the year nearest ACE. RV1's file-key check uses only names whose sole year sits right before ACE, so it cannot catch this.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212c/import/t4-key.mjs (output in t4-key.out) prints: '"PB2027 2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx" -> asked: ["⚠ 2027ACE is already loaded and LOCKED. … Replace it…"]'; '"BES2028 from 2026 ACE.xlsx" -> asked: [] | held: [… ["2028ACE","BES2028 from 2026 ACE.xlsx"]]'; '"2025-11-03 2026 SUST ACE…" -> … ["2025ACE", …]'; 'after OK: 2027ACE is from "PB2027 2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx" … FY2027 kept 0 FY2026 kept 1000000'; 'v2.11 pattern for these names: ["(whole name)","2026","(whole name)"]'.
f.fix: Take the LAST year that can precede ACE by anchoring a greedy prefix: `/^.*(?:^|\D)(20\d\d)(?!\d)(?:.*?[^A-Za-z])?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i`. This gives 2026 for all three names and keeps every name in RV1's check (including '2026-27 ACE' and '2026 SUST ACE 2027 update'). Add 'PB2027 2026 SUST ACE' and '2025-11-03 2026 SUST ACE' to the file-key block.

I could not refute this. I read the code at 41a581d and reproduced the finding with two probes of my own.

**The code.** importAce, line 17825, uses `/(?:^|\D)(20\d\d)(?!\d)(?:.*?[^A-Za-z])?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i`. A regex match starts at the leftmost place it can, and the lazy `.*?` lets any text sit between the year and ACE, including another year. So the FIRST qualifying year wins, not the one nearest ACE.

**Probe 1, the regex alone** (verify-rv1-0-0/regex.mjs). It pulls the pattern out of the board file itself.
- 'PB2027 2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File' gives 2027ACE.
- 'BES2028 from 2026 ACE' gives 2028ACE. v2.11's `/(20\d\d)\s*ACE/i` gave 2026ACE.
- '2025-11-03 2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File' gives 2025ACE.
- A date written as a suffix, or as one run of digits ('20251103 2026 …'), still gives 2026.

**Probe 2, the real importAce** (verify-rv1-0-0/import.mjs). It boots the board in jsdom, builds the workbook with buildXlsx, and starts with 2027ACE loaded and locked.
- The PB2027 name meets "⚠ 2027ACE is already loaded and LOCKED … Replace it". Pressing OK makes 2027ACE hold the 2026 file, with only FY2026 $1,000,000.
- 'BES2028 from 2026 ACE' is filed as a new 2028ACE without asking, and spAce moves to it.
- The date-prefixed name is filed as 2025ACE.
- There were no script errors.

**Is the 'should' documented?** The contract and the guide never say how the key is built from a file name. But the RV1 code comment says "and still the year RIGHT before ACE", and the RV1 check is named "the file key keeps the year right before ACE". R05/R11 also asked for the names v2.11 keyed by year to be restored. 'BES2028 from 2026 ACE' is one of those names: v2.11 keyed it 2026ACE, and v2.12 keys it 2028ACE. So the code breaks the rule its own comment and check state. RV1's check only uses names with one year, so it cannot see this.

**Reachable?** Yes, through Data › Import Annual Cost Estimate… with a file whose name has an earlier four-digit year before the estimate's year. A date prefix such as '2025-11-03' is the most plausible case. 'BES2028 from …' and 'PB2027 …' are less likely: ORBIT writes cycle tags as PB27, which this pattern does not match.

**Severity.** Minor is right. The status line names the key it filed the estimate under, and the locked-replace question names both files, so a careful reader can catch it.

**The proposed fix** (a greedy `^.*` prefix) gives 2026 for all three names. It gives the same answer as today for every name in RV1's check, and for '2026-27 ACE' and '2026 SUST ACE 2027 update'.

f.title: A WBS heading whose parent two rows give differently is settled silently by row order: the same file gives the ECU line to AV or to PSM depending on which row comes first, and no conflict is named
f.area: RV1 E-suffix carry (R03/R09/R26/K08) and the AV + PSM split
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceTree() put(): when a node already exists it keeps its first `up` and compares only names (`if(n && !aceNameSame(n, o.n))`). A second row that puts the same code under a different parent changes nothing and is never reported.
f.scenario: A Full Fund estimate has three rows. P6.2.2.1 (CES3 Propulsion). P6.2.2.1E (CES3 Propulsion, CES4 Engine shop ECU). P6.2.2.1.3E (CES3 ECU Propulsion, CES4 Engine shop ECU). The two E rows disagree about P6.2.2.1E's parent: one says Propulsion, the other ECU Propulsion. AV's requirement is on P6.2.2 and PSM's on the ECU heading P6.2.2E, which the picker offers. With the parent row first, the ECU heading P6.2.2E holds nothing (the R26 symptom), both E lines climb to Propulsion, and the tie-out shows PSM $0 and AV $1,450,000. With the child row first, P6.2.2.1E sits under P6.2.2E, and the tie-out shows PSM $450,000 and AV $1,000,000. Both times the report lists no conflict. Brad's rule (item 132) is that a disagreement is flagged, never silently picked.

Child first: 'P6.2.2.1E {…"up":"P6.2.2E"}', 'conflicts: []', 'split … PSM …$450,000 … AV …$1,000,000'. The same file and rows, in a different order. f.fix: In aceTree's put(), when the node exists and `o.up !== up`, record the disagreement in the conflicts list (for example `{ap, code:c, n:o.n, also:[{n:'under '+up, rows:[row]}]}`, or a separate `upConflicts` drawn in the report), so it is named. For a stable choice, keep the parent an unsuffixed-equivalent rule would give, not the first row's.

**What the code does.** aceTree builds the tree from the kept rows in file order: unsuffixed rows first, then suffixed ones. In put(), when a code already exists, the node keeps the `up` it was created with. Only the name is compared (`if(n && !aceNameSame(n, o.n))`). A second row giving the same code a different parent changes nothing and adds nothing to `conf`.

**The two orders.**
- Rows P6.2.2.1 (CES3 Propulsion), P6.2.2.1E (CES3 Propulsion, CES4 Engine shop ECU) and P6.2.2.1.3E (CES3 ECU Propulsion, CES4 Engine shop ECU).
- **Parent row first:**
  - P6.2.2.1E sits under P6.2.2, and P6.2.2E has no children.
  - P6.2.2.1.3E's path reads "… › Propulsion › Engine shop ECU › Tooling ECU", against its own row's CES3 "ECU Propulsion".
  - With AV on P6.2.2 and PSM on P6.2.2E, the split is PSM $0, AV $1,450,000.
- **Child row first:**
  - P6.2.2.1E sits under P6.2.2E.
  - P6.2.2.1E's path reads "… › ECU Propulsion › Engine shop ECU", against its own row's CES3 "Propulsion".
  - The split is PSM $450,000, AV $1,000,000.
- Both orders: rep.conflicts is [], rep.named is [], and the report's "A paragraph two rows name differently" section is not drawn. The status line says every dollar is kept or in a reason.

**Controls.**
- **Plain rows, same inconsistency:** P6.2.2.1.3, whose CES3 "ECU Propulsion" disagrees with P6.2.2.1's "Propulsion", IS named: a conflict on P6.2.2.
- **Consistent E rows:** when the child E row agrees with its parent E row, both orders give one tree and the same split.

So a suffix turns an inconsistency the plain path flags into a silent choice made by row order.

**Is it in scope?** Item 132 (Brad, 28 Oct): "a paragraph two rows name differently is flagged, never silently picked". Here the two rows name P6.2.2.1E's level-3 heading differently, and one row's own CES name is silently contradicted by the printed path. That is the same disagreement the plain-row control flags.

RV1's own comment on aceTree calls this shape a defect: "the ECU heading … held nothing, the path printed the wrong location and no conflict was named" (R03/R26). The R03 skeptic vote already noted "put() then keeps the first `up` a code was given and says nothing". RV1 added the `on` carry, and named only name conflicts on a carried heading (notes-RV1.md). The parent disagreement was left open, and no notes file records a decision accepting it.

**Limits.** The contract's line "A suffixed heading inherits the unsuffixed heading's parent" would favour the parent-first result. But RV1 deliberately went past it ("P6.2.2.1.3E -> P6.2.2.1E -> P6.2.2E"), and either way the result depends on row order and is silent.

Reaching it needs an ACE file whose rows disagree with each other. A child row's CES3 must differ from its parent row's. The format allows it, and the conflict rule exists for exactly that kind of file, but no such row has been seen in Brad's file. Minor is the right severity.

f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html <template id="helpDoc"> section data-id="t-ppbe": 'each service the position names takes that year’s discretionary and mandatory figure as its base … Budget Management shows a tagged plan’s base read-only'
f.scenario: Open Help › Budget authority from the PPBE position with a position in the box's default 'One figure per line'. The guide says the base is the position's discretionary and mandatory figure. The board instead divides the one figure by its own base, or reads it all discretionary where the own base is $0, as the fit box and Budget Management say. The guide never says the board's own base is what splits it, or that a blank year reads it all discretionary.
f.evidence: The t-ppbe text (sed on line 2321 of the board) contains no 'one figure' sentence. The R37 commit 56df08b changes only the PPBE box hint (ppBody), baOf and fitOneSay, not helpDoc.
f.fix: Add one sentence to t-ppbe: 'A position logged one figure per line sets each service’s total for the year, and the board’s own base for that service and year divides it between the lanes; with no own base it is discretionary.'

f.title: A board file whose CLIN request is not a list opens blank on v2.12. It opened and drew on v2.11, and the import check lets the file through.
f.area: RV2 wbsBlankOf (render path) + W2 wbsClinMoneyRO + import door
f.where: clinList() (`(c.ask||[]).slice()` for a data-pack CLIN and an added CLIN), now reached on every draw through attLists -> wbsBlankOf -> srcRowsOf(...,only) -> clinSplit; also wbsClinMoneyRO() (`(v||[]).some`), reached through attLists -> wbsStateOf; inboundCheck() checks no CLIN request.
f.scenario: What the person sees: they open a board file in which one prime's CLIN request is stored as a number, true or an object instead of a list. An added CLIN in S.clinNew or a CLIN in the data pack will do, from a hand edit or a damaged transfer. On v2.12 no requirement row is drawn, the posture is empty, and nothing says why. On v2.11 the same file opens and draws; only that prime's CLIN drill fails, and only when opened. inboundCheck returns '' for the file, so Import takes it as well. Steps: build a board with prime P and set S.clinNew.P=[{key:'n1',clin:'0009',ask:5}] (or DATA.clins.P[0].ask=5), save it, then open the saved file in each build. Should: the board draws as v2.11 did (CLAUDE.md: a board that will not open is not recoverable), and the import check refuses a CLIN request that is not a list of amounts.
f.evidence: Probes in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212c/wbs/. p7b-v211.mjs: `board-v211.html | boot errors [] | draws | drill THREW (c.ask || []).slice is not a function | rows drawn: 2` and `prioritization-board-grid.html | boot errors ["Uncaught [TypeError: (c.ask || []).slice is not a function]"] | render THREW ... | rows drawn: 0`. p7c-base.mjs (the CLIN request planted in the data pack): v2.11 `door: "" | draws | rows 2`; v2.12 `door: "" | render THREW (c.ask || []).slice is not a function | rows 0`. p7-odd-clin.mjs: the same for a number, {} and true; c23e8a0 (W2 before RV2) already throws, at `(v || []).some is not a function`. p7d-stack.mjs: render and wbsBlankOf throw in clinList, and once that is fixed wbsStateOf still throws in wbsClinMoneyRO.
f.fix: Three changes. (1) Read a request only when it is a list: in clinList use `ask:(Array.isArray(m.ask)? m.ask.slice() : (Array.isArray(c.ask)? c.ask.slice() : []))`, and the same for clinNew rows; in wbsClinMoneyRO use `return (Array.isArray(v)? v : []).some(...)`. (2) Wrap the srcRowsOf call inside wbsBlankOf in try/catch, so a read that fails gives an empty reading and never stops a draw. (3) Have the import check refuse a CLIN `ask` (clinNew[].ask, clinMeta[pid][key].ask, a data pack's clins[].ask) that is not a list of amounts, naming the CLIN.

votes.why:
I reproduced this with my own probes, and v2.12 at 41a581d does what the finding says. The probes are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212c/verify-rv2-0-0/q1.mjs, q1b.mjs and q2.mjs. The v2.11 board is board-v211.html in the same folder, taken from git at bbb7ee9.

**Method.** I built a board on v2.12 with an OGC A and a prime P, then planted a CLIN request that is not a list. I saved it with buildSavedHtml(), put its pubState into each build and booted both.

**Control.** With `ask:[5]`, both builds draw 2 rows, the door returns '', and render does not throw.

**Added CLIN, `S.clinNew.P[0].ask` set to 5, true or {}:**
- v2.11: no boot errors, 2 rows, the posture and the RECORD panel are drawn, and the opening status line shows.
- v2.12: the boot throws "Uncaught TypeError: (c.ask || []).slice is not a function". It draws 0 rows, an empty posture, an empty RECORD panel and an empty status line, so nothing says why.

**Added CLIN, ask set to the text '5':** v2.12 throws instead at "(v || []).some is not a function", which is wbsClinMoneyRO. v2.11 draws.

**Base CLIN in the data pack, `clins.P[0].ask` set to 5:** the same split. v2.11 draws 2 rows, v2.12 draws 0 and throws in clinList.

**The import check.** inboundCheck returns '' for every one of these files. In the same file, a requirement whose ask is "abc" is refused with "the amounts at …dataPack.items[0].ask are not a list of figures". So the door reads this file and has no rule for a CLIN request.

**The code at 41a581d.**
- render() calls scoreboard() before it draws the rows.
- scoreboard() calls attLists(T), which calls wbsBlankOf().
- wbsBlankOf() runs srcRowsOf → clinSplit → clinList for every prime. clinList does `(c.ask||[]).slice()` on both data-pack CLINs and added CLINs.
- attLists also calls wbsStateOf → wbsClinMoneyRO, which does `(v||[]).some`.
- There is no try/catch on that path, so one bad CLIN stops every draw. v2.11 only reached clinList when the CLIN drill was opened.
- A non-list `S.clinMeta[pid][key].ask` is harmless, because both readers check Array.isArray there; my meta-num variant draws on v2.12.

**Is it reachable?** Only through a hand-edited or damaged file. Every CLIN writer in v1.87, v2.11 and v2.12 stores a list. CLAUDE.md treats exactly that kind of file as one the board must cope with ("a hand edit or a damaged transfer is all it takes", item 21's door, the hostile suite). It also says errors degrade rather than throw, because "a board that will not open is not" recoverable. v2.07 fixed two defects of the same kind: malformed side-store data that stopped every redraw.

**Notes and severity.** I found nothing in recovery/v212/notes-*.md or the contract that accepts this. "Major" is arguable, since the file itself is not lost or overwritten. It is still a real v2.12 regression: a file that opens on v2.11 opens blank on v2.12, with no explanation.

**On the fix.** Part (1), reading a request only when it is a list in clinList (base and added) and in wbsClinMoneyRO, covers every variant. A try/catch inside wbsBlankOf alone would not cover the text '5' case, which throws in wbsStateOf.
votes.corrected: The scope is slightly narrower than the finding states. Two places break the draw: `clinNew[].ask`, and a data pack's `clins[].ask`, when either holds a number, true or an object. A text value such as '5' also breaks it, through wbsClinMoneyRO's `(v||[]).some`. `clinMeta[pid][key].ask` does not break anything, because both readers check Array.isArray there. The file on disk is never changed, so nothing is lost; the board just does not draw it.

- A non-list clinMeta[pid][key].ask does not crash: both readers test Array.isArray first. Refusing it at the door is optional hardening.
- A text request such as 'abc' passes .slice in clinList and fails in wbsClinMoneyRO, so the guard is needed there as well.
- Fix (1) also cures the v2.11 drill throw, which was already there before v2.12.
votes.corrected:

f.title: The ACE tie-out's AV + PSM split still claims WBS paragraphs no other surface reads: a prime switched to OGC, an OGC switched to prime, and a removed CLIN
f.area: RV2 aceWbsOf (W1 tie-out) vs the one rule RV2 made for wbsStateOf / srcWbsParts
f.where: aceWbsOf(): for every requirement it reads both wbsReq(id) and every key of S.clinWbs[id], whatever the type. That includes a prime's hidden requirement-level paragraph, an OGC's leftover CLIN paragraphs, and the WBS of a CLIN removed in the drill (kept so it can be put back). wbsStateOf, wbsUnlistedOf, srcWbsParts and the edit box read a prime's listed CLINs only, and a non-prime's own lines only.
f.scenario: O&M board with A (AV, OGC, on 1.3), P (PSM, a prime, CLIN 0001 on 1.2.2) and O (PSM, an OGC, on 1.2.1). Each estimate line is $1M and is filed under the ACE's AV. Switch P to OGC and O to prime in the edit box. The Spend Plan Source then sends P's $300 and O's $200 with the WBS blank, Needs attention lists P ('no paragraph') and O ('USAF money on no CLIN'), and the edit box shows P with no WBS. Yet the tie-out's split still shows PSM claiming $2M of estimate lines, through paragraphs no screen shows. The same happens for a prime whose CLIN 0002 (on 1.2.1) is removed in the drill: the file sends nothing on 1.2.1, and PSM still claims that $1M line. Should: PSM claims only 1.2.2 ($1M), and the 1.2.1 line no office claims stays on the shared line. RV2's notes name the type case and leave it for the lead; the removed-CLIN case is not named anywhere.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212c/wbs/p6-type-switch.mjs: after reqApply(P,{ptype:'OGC'}) and reqApply(O,{ptype:'PRIME'}): `Needs attention ▦: [["P",300,["no paragraph"]],["O",200,["USAF money on no CLIN"]]]`, `Spend Plan Source lines: [["A",100,"1.3 - Training"],["P",300,""],["O",200,""]]`, `edit box for P: WBS field ""`, `aceWbsOf [["1.2.2"],["1.2.1"]]`, `AV + PSM split: {"AV":1000000,"PSM":2000000,"shared":0}`. p6b-removed-clin.mjs: `Spend Plan Source [["A","",100,"1.3 - Training"],["P","0001",300,"1.2.2 - Depot"]]`, CLINs on the board `["0001"]`, `aceWbsOf(P) ["1.2.2","1.2.1"]`, `split {"AV":1000000,"PSM":2000000,"shared":0}`.
f.fix: Have aceWbsOf read the one rule the other surfaces read: `wbsStateOf(id).lines.map(e=>wbsCodeIn(e&&e.w)).filter(...)` (a prime: its listed CLINs only, via clinListRO; otherwise the requirement's own lines). The paragraph stays stored and is kept for a restore.
